To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the market reaction to the introduction of the enhanced voting rights in Italy was negative, with a significant drop of the stock price on the announcement day; 2) the market reaction was stronger for companies with higher levels of institutional ownership and for companies that had a higher number of shareholders; 3) the market reaction is consistent with a change in the corporate governance system of these companies, which are now more likely to experience a change of control.

the introduction of super voting shares has a significant impact on the share price, and that this effect is more pronounced for companies in which the super voting shareholders have a controlling interest.

(a) the introduction of the enhanced voting rights is associated with a significant increase in stock prices, and (b) this increase in stock prices is significantly larger when the enhanced voting rights are introduced through the conversion of existing voting shares into enhanced voting shares than when they are introduced through the issuance of new enhanced voting shares.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the impact on share prices of a recent legislative innovation, introduced in Italy by the 24 June 2014 Legislative Decree no. 91, which has the purpose of strengthening the protection of minority shareholders.
the analysis of the effects on the market of the introduction of super-voting shares.
the effects of a change in the voting rights regime in Italy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the introduction of the enhanced voting rights is an effective and efficient tool to protect the minority shareholders, in particular in the event of a change in control, and to prevent the abuse of the majority shareholder.

the introduction of the enhanced voting rights in the Italian corporate law, which was a response to the need of the shareholders to have a more effective control over the company, was not followed by the market by a positive response.
the Italian government has taken a step in the right direction, but that there is still a long way to go to reach the goal of a more effective corporate governance in Italy.
